affected_system: public digital services, identity, applications, appointments, and assisted access
alternatives: rank verified high-consequence candidates for accessible administrative service redesign portfolio
select a risk-, equity-, and lifecycle-balanced portfolio for accessible administrative service redesign portfolio
pair journey-friction, equity, risk, privacy, and lifecycle prioritization with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Page events, applications, errors, appointments, contacts, decisions, and outcomes remain distinct.
No automated score determines eligibility, enforcement, or denial without lawful human review.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: fund only already-committed work for accessible administrative service redesign portfolio.

constraints.description: The digital public access and administrative service delivery prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: chief digital officer and administrative service delivery director
decision_question: Which identity, form, language, accessibility, integration, support, and privacy improvements should be funded?
family_title: Digital public access and administrative service delivery

independence_key.binding_constraint: The digital public access and administrative service delivery prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for accessible administrative service redesign portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: journey-friction, equity, risk, privacy, and lifecycle prioritization
independence_key.primary_outcome: verified user effort and preventable service failure

intended_claim: A versioned prioritize design for comparing declared alternatives affecting accessible administrative service redesign portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: verified user effort and preventable service failure
distributional gap in verified user effort and preventable service failure
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report modeled time savings as realized uptake, eligibility, or resident welfare.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for accessible administrative service redesign portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.

title: Prioritize accessible public-service redesign
transportability_risks: Eligibility, identity, language, disability access, connectivity, trust, and service design differ.
Digital telemetry omits non-users and can encode device or tracking coverage.
